newsitem.title: UK: CWC confirms partial flotation at 1330 GMT.
newsitem.headline: CWC confirms partial flotation at 1330 GMT.

text.p: Cable and Wireless Communications (CWC), Britain's new cable telephone and television giant, confirmed on Monday that it expected to float a 14.7 percent stake at 1330 GMT on both the London and New York stock exchanges.

Just over 1.489 billion shares will be available in CWC, which was formed by the four-way merger of Cable and Wireless Plc's Mercury unit with the three UK cable television units of NYNEX Corp and Bell Canada International, a stock exchange spokesman said.

Analysts, who value the new cable company at an average of around 4.5 billion pounds ($7.3 billion), are keen to see the market price CWC, which will be the main rival to British Telecommunications Plc.
North American shareholders have overwhelmingly approved the recommended share offer in the new company, with over 90 percent of votes cast in favour.
"We are now set to introduce Cable & Wireless Communications as a major force in the UK market," CWC chief executive Graham Wallace said in a statement.
The share offer is too small to propel CWC, which comprises Mercury, NYNEX CableComms Group, Bell Cablemedia Plc and Videotron into the FTSE index in London.
